summary: Collapse Settings > About > Diagnostics behind a disclosure that previews its own contents, remembers the user's choice, and opens itself on a translated build the user has never answered for, while the amber gist keeps that warning visible after a deliberate close.

reactNativeIos.reason: The React Native client has no About or diagnostics surface. `getDiagnostics` is an Electron-only IPC handler reading Electron process metrics and GPU feature status, and apps/mobile never calls it: there is no occurrence of getDiagnostics or a diagnostics screen anywhere under apps/mobile/src.

nativeAndroid.reason: The native Android client has no About or diagnostics surface. Its ui package contains no settings-about screen that renders host process metrics, and nothing in apps/android calls the diagnostics contract.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema change and no migration. The open/closed preference is one row in the existing key-value `settings` table under `about.diagnosticsExpanded`. An absent key already means 'no preference' and resolves to collapsed, so an older database and an older client both behave correctly with no backfill, and a newer database is readable by an older client that simply ignores the key.

updateRelease.reason: Renderer presentation change only. No package identity, signing, deep-link scheme, update channel, IPC channel, or wire-protocol change; the diagnostics IPC contract and its payload are untouched.

automated: npm run typecheck passed for both the main and renderer projects; eslint --max-warnings=0 passed on both changed TypeScript files, which is what the pre-commit hook runs on staged files.
npm test passed 378 files / 3,616 tests with 3 skipped on this branch, including 19 disclosure-policy tests and 11 first-frame render tests.

tests/unit/diagnostics-disclosure.test.ts pins the gist text, the singular/plural and unknown-count terminal cases, the shared footprint formula, and the preference precedence: a translated build opens for an unanswered user, and a deliberate close is respected.

tests/unit/diagnostics-section-render.test.ts renders the real component with renderToStaticMarkup and asserts the first frame is collapsed (aria-expanded=false, grid-template-rows:0fr, body inert, no process rows) and that hover and focus are class-driven rather than imperative.

An adversarial review of the branch diff was run and its two substantive findings were fixed: a pre-snapshot click could suppress the translated override for the session, and the persisted collapse choice was discarded on every reopen for a translated build. Both are resolved by the preference precedence change. Focus restoration on collapse, the class-based hover and focus ring, the shared footprint formula, the error colour on the collapsed gist, and an unmount guard on the diagnostics read were also applied.
notExercised: The collapse and expand animation, the chevron rotation, and the hover and focus rings have not been watched by a human in the running app.
The translated/Rosetta path has not been exercised on an x64 build running under Apple silicon translation; it is covered by unit tests only, because this host runs the native arm64 build.

Persistence across an app restart, and the settings read and write themselves, are not covered by an effect-running test: the unit harness is node-environment with no jsdom, so renderToStaticMarkup runs no effects. Only the key name and the pure precedence rule are pinned.
Focus restoration on collapse is implemented but not asserted by a test, for the same harness reason.
Behaviour under prefers-reduced-motion has not been verified visually.

tests/unit/tcp-host.test.ts timed out once at its 5s limit during an early full-suite run and passed in isolation and on every later run; it is a real-socket test and load-sensitive, and it is unrelated to this change.
